A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhysioWave and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained and relocated material can be matched reliably. Internal inconsistencies in v3 affect interpretation of some changes, but do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original ECG and EMG benchmark results, multimodal classification experiments, ablations, and reconstruction and representation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, EEG sleep staging, PPG classification and regression, learned-filter analyses, and ECG GradCAM results.

M1.justification: Appendix A.7 introduces an enhanced EEG variant with multi-scale convolutions, cross-channel attention, and window attention. Figure 1 and Tables 12–13 also change the reconstruction architecture specification from v2's eight-layer Transformer decoder to a reconstruction head, although Section 2.3 retains the decoder description. The underlying wavelet, masking, and multimodal fusion formulations remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained ECG/EMG classification and multimodal emotion/driving tasks, v3 adds five-class EEG sleep staging on Sleep-EDF and PPG-based activity recognition and heart-rate regression on PPG-DaLiA (Appendices A.7–A.8). These substantially extend the evaluated modalities and task requirements.

E2.justification: The original benchmark comparator sets are retained. New comparisons include BENDR, BIOT, LaBraM, and EEGPT for Sleep-EDF; Pulse-PPG for activity recognition; and Pulse-PPG, Deep PPG, and NAS-PPG for heart-rate regression (Tables 9–11). These introduce substantial additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: Compared with v2 Appendix C, v3 Appendix D explicitly omits band-pass/notch filtering, changes ECG windows from 1024 to 2048 samples, and selects eight EMG channels instead of padding to sixteen. Table 12 also changes the ECG wavelet candidates. New EEG/PPG experiments introduce additional model configurations, scratch training, and task-specific metrics. Section 3.1 retains conflicting earlier preprocessing descriptions, so these are reported setting revisions without evidence establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 adds component combinations, hard/Gumbel/soft gating comparisons, FFN variants, and wavelet initialization/selection studies (Tables 4–8). It also adds learned-filter diagnostics and ECG GradCAM case studies with an analysis of 100 samples per class (F.1 and F.4). The original masking/pretraining ablation and EPN-612 visual analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Figure 5 adds error bars to the multimodal comparisons previously shown without them in v2 Figures 5–6. However, neither the figure nor the new checklist defines the bars or supplies run counts, seeds, or an estimation procedure. Additional experimental runs therefore cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results, but several multimodal baseline bar values change; for example, TPRO-Net arousal is plotted near 85% in v2 and 88% in v3. Tables 4–11 add substantial results, including enhanced EEG balanced accuracy of 0.7312, PPG activity F1 of 0.5952, and heart-rate MAE of 5.22 versus Pulse-PPG's 3.705. These are revised or newly reported results, rather than established same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The method equations and Algorithm 1 are unchanged after matching formatting and page moves. The new 'Mathematical Properties Validation' section reports empirical filter norms, support, frequency characteristics, and correlations; it adds no formal definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims: wavelet-based representation learning with frequency-guided masking, large-scale EMG/ECG pretraining, and multimodal integration with pretrained EEG encoders. The additional appendix evidence does not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations that learned filters replace manual denoising and beneficially depart from classical wavelet constraints, and that GradCAM localization supports clinical relevance and diagnostic suitability (D, F.1, F.4). Appendix A also interprets modality generalization and model-size/performance tradeoffs. The earlier limitations concerning underexplored EEG/PPG and incomplete universality remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds a repository address and statements that code and preprocessing scripts are released. It documents reconstruction-head activation, dropout, normalization and dimensions, new EEG/PPG configurations, and EMG channel-selection criteria. These materially expand and revise reproducibility information, although the repository's contents cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting the sleep/PPG experiments, wavelet properties, GradCAM, and clinical interpretation. It removes the MERL-associated and MaeFE references while retaining those baseline rows in Table 1. The existing related-work discussion and central novelty positioning remain largely intact; bibliographic metadata updates do not constitute additional substantive changes.

P1.justification: Local language edits and rewritten preprocessing passages accompany author/venue updates, a new Ethics Statement and checklist, and insertion of Additional Experiments before the retained appendices. The main narrative and relative order of existing sections remain largely unchanged, so the added scientific content does not amount to extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adds eight experimental tables and new learned-filter and GradCAM figures, redraws Figure 1, and merges the multimodal charts into a redesigned two-panel Figure 5 with error bars. Result tables gain colored ranking highlights. Existing reconstruction and EPN-612 plots are relocated and renumbered, rather than newly added.

improvement.justification: The component ablations and EEG/PPG studies substantially strengthen areas weakly validated in v2, and the added access information helps reproducibility. However, v3 introduces unresolved contradictions: its reconstruction-head specifications conflict with Section 2.3, and its revised filtering and channel-selection procedures conflict with Section 3.1 while headline scores remain unchanged. The new error bars are also undefined. These evidence gains and material reproducibility ambiguities prevent a reliable net judgment of overall quality.
